lead: >-
  La Azulita is a mountain settlement in Mérida state in the Venezuelan Andes. A current 12-day Ada Tours itinerary passes through it on day 9, after overnight observation of Catatumbo lightning near Lake Maracaibo and before continuing toward the savannas of Los Llanos. This stage includes a waterfall, a cave, lunch in the village and a road through cloud forest. Discover how the journey works, how much time is allocated to La Azulita and what kind of trip is suitable for exploring the area.
---

## Which tour passes through La Azulita?

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which [La Azulita](/venezuela/place/la-azulita/) forms part of the **main itinerary**. In the current selection, the visit is one stage of a longer journey through the Andes, rather than a separate multi-day stay in the settlement.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_krasota_venesuely}}

The [“Venezuela in 12 Days: Beaches and Eco-Routes” tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/) connects [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/), [Choroní](/venezuela/place/choroni/), [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), [Mérida](/venezuela/place/merida/), [Lake Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/), La Azulita and [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/). The idea is to explore Venezuela's different natural zones, from the Caribbean coast to mountain forests and plains.

**La Azulita is visited on day 9.** After spending the night in the Catatumbo area, travelers return by boat to the port, then drive toward the Andes through the settlement. The itinerary includes a local waterfall and cave, lunch and the onward journey through cloud forest. This sequence makes it a different experience from spending a holiday in one mountain town.

## What happens in La Azulita on day nine?

First, the group finishes the waterborne stage near [Lake Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/). The itinerary includes a boat outing to observe birds and river dolphins, after which travelers return to camp and continue overland.

The next stage passes through [La Azulita](/venezuela/place/la-azulita/), a small Andean settlement in Mérida state. The road winds among green hillsides. Stops at **Pirate Cave and La Azulita Waterfall** are scheduled, followed by lunch in the village. The vehicle then climbs toward cloud forest and mountain settlements.

This is a day built around the road and its stops. There is no separate overnight stay in La Azulita, and the source itinerary does not include an extensive hiking expedition along all the surrounding trails. If you want to spend several days in the village exploring local crafts, birds and mountain routes, you will need a different kind of trip.

## Why La Azulita is interesting on the route from Maracaibo to the Andes

The settlement lies in the Andrés Bello municipality amid the mountains of Mérida state. Humid hillsides and stretches of cloud forest surround it. Near Lake Maracaibo, waterways and wetlands dominate the scenery; climbing into the Andes brings changes in temperature, vegetation and the views along the road.

The contrast between successive days is particularly memorable. On the previous night, the group is in the low-lying Catatumbo area observing lightning. The next road journey takes in settlements, mountain waterfalls and forests. Later stages bring highlands and savannas. La Azulita lets travelers experience this geographical transition firsthand.

The village itself offers mountain architecture and the Church of the Immaculate Conception. But the fact that these places appear **on the destination page** does not mean that every tour passing through includes them. Ada Tours' confirmed itinerary specifies the waterfall, cave and lunch; other local visits must be arranged separately.

Read more about the nature, architecture and settlement on the [La Azulita destination page](/venezuela/place/la-azulita/). Our catalog lets you choose a tour that includes this stop.

## How La Azulita connects Catatumbo and Los Llanos

It makes sense to assess the visit alongside days 8–11.

| Day | Main stage |
|---|---|
| 8 | [Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/), Catatumbo |
| 9 | [La Azulita](/venezuela/place/la-azulita/), Andes |
| 10 | Transfer to [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/) |
| 11 | Safari in Los Llanos |

On day 8, the group heads to the southwestern part of Maracaibo, settles into a camp and observes **Catatumbo lightning** in the evening. The lake region has an exceptionally high incidence of thunderstorms: its terrain and humid air favor storm formation. But the number of visible flashes on a particular night cannot be predicted.

On day 9, the route continues from La Azulita through cloud forest and highland areas toward the overnight stop. Days 10–11 focus on the [plains of Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/), overland and water excursions with local guides and wildlife observation.

La Azulita is therefore part of the **transition from lake lowlands to the Andes and savannas**. The tour suits travelers who want to see all these landscapes during one holiday.

## The complete itinerary: beaches, Canaima, Andes and savannas

The 12-day program begins by the sea. Travelers drive from Caracas to [Choroní](/venezuela/place/choroni/) for beach days. Then come a flight and an introduction to [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), a lagoon outing and a trip to Angel Falls.

Afterward, the route passes through [Mérida](/venezuela/place/merida/) toward Maracaibo. The Catatumbo stage includes boat trips and a night in hammocks. La Azulita and the mountain road follow, then Los Llanos. The trip ends with a return to Caracas.

This is an extensive **12-day private tour** across several climatic zones, with changes of accommodation. Travelers interested only in the mountains around Mérida may find the wider itinerary excessive. For those wanting to explore Venezuela as a whole, it offers beaches, tepuis, rivers, cloud forests, highlands and savannas.

## Driving, physical demands and itinerary conditions

**Transfers.** Day nine begins by boat and continues by road through the mountains. The confirmed description does not state exactly how many hours each traveler will spend in La Azulita. Do not expect an entire independent sightseeing day devoted to this settlement.

**Natural conditions.** Temperatures and rainfall change as the journey climbs from lowlands to mountain forests. For stops by water and on mountain roads, comfortable non-slip shoes, rain protection and warmer clothing than on the coast will be useful. Visiting times and access to natural areas depend on weather.

**Accommodation and services.** The [12-day tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/) lists accommodation, private transfers, domestic flights, meals according to the itinerary, excursions and a Russian-speaking guide. Optional excursions, transatlantic flights and certain expenses are listed separately. Refer to the full tour page for the exact inclusions and current price, and do not apply those terms to other products.

**Who it suits.** The itinerary involves long travel days, boat journeys, a hike at Angel Falls and a nighttime nature excursion near Maracaibo. It is aimed at travelers who enjoy a packed sequence of different regions. Those preferring a leisurely mountain stay should compare the [Venezuela tours catalog](/venezuela/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours through La Azulita

### On which day is La Azulita visited?

On **day 9** of the [12-day Venezuela itinerary](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/), after observing Catatumbo lightning overnight and before continuing through the Andes toward Barinas.

### Is there an overnight stay in La Azulita itself?

No separate night in the village is listed on the current itinerary. Day nine includes stops, lunch and onward travel. Distinguish passing through La Azulita from a trip that includes accommodation there.

### What exactly is planned during the visit?

The itinerary names La Azulita Waterfall, Pirate Cave and lunch in the village. The route then continues through cloud forest and other Andean settlements.

### Can La Azulita be combined with Catatumbo lightning observation?

Yes. On [this itinerary](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/), the visits follow one another: Catatumbo and Maracaibo on day 8, La Azulita on day 9. A nighttime thunderstorm is a natural phenomenon, not a guaranteed scheduled event.

### Is the itinerary suitable only for a mountain holiday?

Its defining feature is the combination of the coast, Canaima, the Andes and Los Llanos. If you mainly want mountain walks and several nights in one place, compare other tours and explore [Mérida](/venezuela/place/merida/) and [La Azulita](/venezuela/place/la-azulita/) separately.

## Laime viewpoint: Angel Falls from the ground

Mirador Laime is a viewpoint in Canaima National Park overlooking the famous [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) on the rock wall of Auyán-tepui. To reach it, travelers generally take a river journey by boat before hiking through damp tropical forest.

The main attraction at Laime is the view from near the base of the mountain toward a waterfall almost a kilometer high. In clear weather, a slender stream of water stands out against the vast, dark tepui wall. Clouds and rainfall, however, constantly change visibility.

## Where Laime is and how to reach it

From the village and [Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/place/canaima-lagoon/), the journey first follows the [Carrao River](/venezuela/place/carrao-river/) and then the [Churún](/venezuela/place/churun-river/). The group reaches the [Ratonsito](/venezuela/place/ratoncito-island/) area, where boats stop for the hiking stage. The walk toward Laime begins here.

The trail winds through forest with tree roots, streams, stones and wet patches. Mosses, ferns, bromeliads and other tropical plants grow nearby. Rain can make the ground slippery, so wear closed shoes with good grip.

The four-day Ada Tours itinerary allows approximately one hour for the walk to Laime. This is an estimate for the specific route; the actual time can change with weather, water levels and trail conditions.

## What Angel Falls looks like from here

Angel Falls has a total height of approximately **979 m**, and much of its water drops almost vertically from Auyán-tepui. From below, the contrast between the gigantic cliff, forest and slender white stream is particularly striking.

During the wetter months the flow is usually stronger, although heavy clouds can hide the upper edge. In drier periods the water sometimes disperses into a fine mist and the river approach needs separate assessment. For this reason, reaching the viewpoint does not guarantee the same panorama on every date.

The viewpoint lies **at the foot of the mountain range, not on the summit of the tepui**. Ascending Auyán-tepui belongs to a different category of expedition. A standard walk to Laime does not include climbing to the summit.

## Who was Laime?

The name honors Aleksandrs Laime, a traveler of Latvian origin who explored the Angel Falls region in the twentieth century. In Spanish-language descriptions, the viewpoint is called Mirador Laime. His name remains attached to this panoramic stop on the route from the Churún River.

It is useful to distinguish three places: **Ratonsito** is the river stop, **Laime** the forest viewpoint, and **Angel Falls** the waterfall itself. These names refer to different stages of one excursion.

## Preparing for the hike

The approach follows a natural trail, so comfortable footwear, water and rain protection matter more than ordinary city walking clothes. In a humid climate, expect slippery roots and stones even if it was not raining earlier that day.

River conditions may require the boat journey to be shortened or changed. Whether the hiking section is possible depends on reaching the landing site safely. Guides determine the route and stops; do not leave the path to take a different photograph.

After Laime, the excursion usually returns to the river and then to Canaima. It is a mistake to plan it as a short walk directly from the village.

## Laime in the Ada Tours program

On [“Venezuelan Beauty: Canaima and Angel Falls in 4 Days”](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/), day two is devoted to the Carrao and Churún river journey and the walk to Laime. It includes the river expedition, tropical forest trail and return to Canaima. Another day covers the lagoon and [Sapo Falls](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/).

The itinerary suits travelers who want to see Angel Falls from the ground, rather than only in photographs or from an aircraft. Access to the viewpoint and visibility depend on actual weather and river conditions.

## Frequently asked questions about Laime viewpoint

### Is Laime the same as Angel Falls?

No. Laime is a viewpoint from which you can see the cliff and the waterfall.

### Can you drive to Laime?

The usual route begins with a boat journey and ends with a hike. It is not a roadside viewpoint.

### How long does the climb take?

The four-day Ada Tours program estimates about an hour on foot from the landing area. Actual timing depends on trail conditions.

### Is Angel Falls visible in the rain?

The flow may be stronger, but heavy rain and clouds can obscure the upper part. Visibility on a particular day is not guaranteed.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_venezuela_canaima_angel_falls_4_days}}

## Reaching Laime: boat, forest trail and a view of Angel Falls

The excursion begins in [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). After a ground transfer to the boat landing, visitors travel along the [Carrao River](/venezuela/place/carrao-river/) and then the [Churún River](/venezuela/place/churun-river/) toward [Devil's Canyon](/venezuela/place/canaima-devils-canyon/). They disembark near [Ratonsito Island](/venezuela/place/ratoncito-island/) and continue on foot through humid tropical forest.

According to the dedicated Laime description, **the walking section takes approximately one hour**. Streams, moss-covered stones, orchids and bromeliads appear along the path. At the end, the trail opens onto views of [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) and the steep walls of the tepui. The return walk, boat journeys and lunch stop make for a lengthy day: allowing only an hour of walking time would underestimate the total outing.

The complete standalone excursion is described on the [“Angel Falls in One Day: Carrao, Churún, Ratonsito and Laime” page](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/angel-falls-full-day/). It takes place on day two of the four-day tour, after an introduction to Canaima on day one.

## What you see from the viewpoint and why the waterfall's height matters

Angel Falls plunges from the edge of Auyán-tepui. Its height is around **979 meters**, and a substantial part of the falling water disperses in the air. It is among the most recognizable landscapes of Canaima National Park, which was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1994.

Laime allows visitors to see the waterfall from the ground after following a forest path. The experience depends on water levels, cloud cover and visibility: low clouds may obscure the upper cliffs, and the flow changes with the seasons. A scheduled viewpoint visit does not guarantee clear skies or an identical view on every date.

A flight above Angel Falls offers another perspective and is classified as **an optional excursion** on the current four-day program. It does not replace the included day of river travel and hiking.

## Laime, Canaima Lagoon and Sapo: different parts of the trip

On a short journey, travelers see several contrasting waterscapes. The way each is visited makes the differences clear.

| Place | Activity |
|---|---|
| [Laime](/venezuela/place/laime-viewpoint/) | Hike through forest for a view of Angel Falls |
| [Canaima Lagoon](/venezuela/place/canaima-lagoon/) | Boat ride near the waterfalls |
| [Sapo Falls](/venezuela/place/sapo-falls/) | Exploring a waterfall by the lagoon |
| [Ratonsito](/venezuela/place/ratoncito-island/) | Landing before the hike |

The first day of the four-day itinerary includes a lagoon excursion and visits to [Sapo and Hacha waterfalls](/venezuela/canaima-and-angel-falls/sapo-hacha-lagoon-trip/). Travelers head toward Angel Falls on day two. Visiting Canaima exclusively for Laime and skipping the lagoon would mean missing another major part of the included itinerary.

## How much time to allow and what to bring

**The whole trip lasts 4 days and 3 nights.** It includes arriving in Canaima, the Angel Falls excursion via Laime, a free day by the lagoon and a flight back to Caracas. The viewpoint day is the most demanding combination of boat travel and walking.

For the forest trail and boat landings, take sturdy-soled shoes, light quick-drying clothes, protection from rain, sun and insects. Protect electronics and documents from moisture. Exact river travel times, opportunities for swimming and the order of stops depend on water levels and conditions along the route.

The current tour offers two accommodation options in Canaima: Tapuy Lodge and Waku Lodge. Check the [four-day tour page](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/) for the particular rate, chosen accommodation and included services. The viewpoint's name alone does not indicate the accommodation category.

## Questions about tours visiting Laime viewpoint

### Can I visit Laime without a long hike?

On the current itinerary, the walk from Ratonsito's landing area takes about an hour each way according to the destination description. But you must first reach the trail by river and then return to Canaima. It is a full excursion day with a substantial boat section.

### Are Laime and Angel Falls the same place?

No. [Laime](/venezuela/place/laime-viewpoint/) is a viewpoint on the approach to [Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). The waterfall is the main natural landmark; the viewpoint is a place to observe it during the excursion.

### On which day is the viewpoint scheduled?

On day two of the [“Canaima and Angel Falls in 4 Days” itinerary](/venezuela/tour/canaima-angel-falls-4-days/). Day one focuses on the lagoon and nearby waterfalls; day three is for relaxation and optional activities.

### Is a helicopter flight over Angel Falls included?

No. The current four-day itinerary lists the flight as a separately paid optional activity. The main excursion to Angel Falls follows rivers and a walking trail to Laime.

### Is the waterfall guaranteed to be visible in every season?

The viewpoint is part of the itinerary, but cloud cover and water levels affect visibility and travel arrangements. There is no guarantee about the weather or intensity of the flow on a particular date.

## Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela: Catatumbo lightning and a nighttime expedition

**Lake Maracaibo (Lago de Maracaibo) lies in western [Venezuela](/venezuela/), in a large lowland basin near the northern foothills of the Andes.** It is internationally famous for the atmospheric phenomenon known as *Relámpago del Catatumbo*: frequent nighttime thunderstorms over the lake's southwestern reaches.

For travelers, the area offers two contrasting experiences: exploring wetland shores and river channels by day, then observing storm clouds after dark. **Lightning is not guaranteed on any particular night**, so the outing is best planned as a nature expedition whose landscapes are worthwhile in themselves, with thunderstorm observation depending on weather.

## Where the lake is and why thunderstorms are so frequent

Maracaibo connects to the Gulf of Venezuela in the north and receives water from numerous rivers. One of them is the **Catatumbo River**, which flows into the southwestern part of the lake, forming an extensive wet delta.

Local geography favors thunderstorm development. The lake's warm waters supply moisture to the air, while mountain ranges surrounding the basin affect airflow. Winds converge over part of the lake at night, potentially forming powerful thunderclouds.

According to satellite research by **NASA**, the Maracaibo region is among the world's most active lightning hotspots in terms of flash density. A scientific paper on global thunderstorm hotspots published in the *Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society* explains the high frequency through the combination of a warm body of water and local wind circulation.

Scientific accounts cite estimates of as many as **297 days per year with characteristic thunderstorm conditions**. This is long-term climate data, not a forecast or a promise of lightning during a particular excursion.

## What is Catatumbo lightning?

Catatumbo is the local name for recurring thunderstorm activity over the lake and the area around the river of the same name. Powerful flashes illuminate the clouds and can be visible from a considerable distance after dark.

Its frequency earned the phenomenon the historic nickname **“Catatumbo Lighthouse.”** Sailors used the light near the horizon for orientation on the lake, although it consists of ordinary electrical discharges within thunderclouds, not a permanent natural beacon.

Watch the phenomenon from a safe location chosen by local guides. Thunderstorms are dangerous on open water and shores: **never remain in a boat beneath a thundercloud just to take photographs**, approach lightning or disregard a guide's decision to stop the excursion.

## The nature of the southwestern lakeshore

The area around the Catatumbo Delta differs from the large urban zones on the northern shore. Wetlands, branching river channels, dense tropical vegetation and places best explored from the water characterize the landscape.

| Time | What to experience |
|---|---|
| Daytime | Lakeside marshes and rivers |
| On the boat | Channels and birdlife |
| Dusk | Light and delta landscapes |
| Night | Possible Catatumbo thunderstorms |

Nature excursions may offer sightings of birds, iguanas, monkeys and other animals inhabiting wetland ecosystems. Wildlife encounters are unpredictable, particularly in poor visibility or with changing water levels. Local guides select accessible channels and explain how to observe animals without disturbing them.

## Maracaibo on a current Ada Tours itinerary

The [12-day “Venezuelan Nature and Beaches” tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/) devotes a separate day to the lake after time in the Andes. Travelers head toward the southwestern part in off-road vehicles with a specialist guide, then continue by riverboat. The main purpose of the day is **to explore Catatumbo's natural environment and attempt to observe a nighttime thunderstorm**.

This route also includes Choroní beaches, Canaima National Park and the savannas of Los Llanos. Lake Maracaibo occupies a different natural zone, adding wetlands, river habitats and a chance to observe the night sky.

When comparing programs, check how much time is allotted to Catatumbo, how the nighttime excursion is arranged and who makes the decision to cancel boat activities during a storm.

## When is the best time to visit?

Seasonal rainfall and thunderstorm patterns vary throughout the year. Some months are especially favorable for lightning, but a high statistical frequency across the region does not mean that storms can be observed every night or from every part of the shore.

For the journey, bring lightweight clothing that covers your skin, insect protection, a waterproof phone case and an extra dry layer. Agree in advance on the schedule, arrangements for nighttime observation and water safety rules.

## Frequently asked questions about Lake Maracaibo

### Why is lightning so frequent over Maracaibo?

Mountains, the warm lake and converging winds create conditions for nighttime thunderstorms. Climate and satellite studies support this explanation.

### Can Catatumbo lightning be seen every evening?

No. The phenomenon is frequent over many years, but a particular night may not have suitable thunderstorms.

### Can I visit for the birds and river wildlife?

Yes. The natural areas along the southwestern shore offer wetland habitats to explore on an arranged boat excursion.

### Is Lake Maracaibo included in any Ada Tours trips?

Yes. The [12-day Venezuela journey](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/) includes a visit to Maracaibo and Catatumbo.

**Maracaibo is scheduled for day 8.** This is a nature expedition to the southwest of the lake, not a city sightseeing walk in Maracaibo. On the morning of day 9, the journey continues toward the Andes.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_krasota_venesuely}}

## Day 8: off-road drive, river and a night near Catatumbo

After breakfast, travelers head toward the lake in 4×4 vehicles with a specialist guide. The route then passes through Santa Rosa to a river stage: the group boards a boat and travels along the waterway. Along the riverside vegetation, visitors may see birds, iguanas, howler monkeys and caimans, locally called “babas.”

By lunchtime the group is scheduled to reach **Palafito camp**. A palafito is a structure raised on stilts above water or wet ground. Lunch follows arrival, with dinner and a nighttime nature safari in the evening. The main aim of the night outing is observing Catatumbo lightning. The itinerary specifies **hammock accommodation** and includes lunch and dinner on day 8.

The next morning, a boat takes the group back toward the road. Dolphin and bird observations are also listed. The drive then continues through [La Azulita](/venezuela/place/la-azulita/) and [Barinas](/venezuela/place/barinas/). The overnight stay beside the water is thus one stage of a longer journey between natural regions, not a separate multi-day lake holiday.

## Why Catatumbo lightning is famous worldwide

Catatumbo lightning is an atmospheric phenomenon near the mouth of the Catatumbo River at Lake Maracaibo. NASA research identifies this area as one of the world's most active regions for lightning strikes. **Nighttime thunderstorms** are frequent here: warm, humid air over the lake interacts with local winds influenced by the surrounding mountains.

Recurring flashes earned the phenomenon the poetic nickname “Catatumbo Lighthouse.” But long-term statistics are not a forecast for your chosen night. Visibility depends on cloud cover, rainfall and actual weather. Even with a high average frequency, lightning observation on a specific date cannot be guaranteed.

For this reason, evaluate both parts of the itinerary: watching for thunderstorms at night and exploring the river and lakeside ecosystems by day. The daytime experience has value even when weather is unpredictable.

## How Maracaibo differs from other stages of the Venezuela tour

These regions belong to one journey but offer very different experiences.

| Destination | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) | Tepuis, rivers and Angel Falls |
| [Mérida](/venezuela/place/merida/) | Mountains and Andean scenery |
| [Lake Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/) | Catatumbo, boats and overnight camp |
| [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/) | Flat savannas and wildlife safaris |

Unlike the mountain route around Mérida, a day near Catatumbo focuses on **wet lowlands and waterways**. It differs from Los Llanos in its primary aim: plains outings concentrate on birds and terrestrial animals, while the lake stage focuses on the nighttime sky and river ecosystems.

If lightning is your only travel goal, assess the road journey and overnight arrangements separately. Our current offering is a [12-day Venezuela itinerary](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/); a short standalone Catatumbo trip cannot be assumed to be a published product simply because the destination is described.

## Preparing for the overnight stay and boat journeys

You will spend part of the day on the water and the night at a nature camp. Pack light long-sleeved clothing, a waterproof jacket, insect protection, shoes with good grip and a watertight case for your phone and documents. Consider in advance whether sleeping in a hammock suits you, particularly if you normally prefer hotel rooms.

Lightning can be spectacular in photographs, but approaching open water for photography during a thunderstorm is dangerous. Follow local guides' instructions and remain in designated safe shelter. The night outing does not guarantee access to every point on the shore: the route and the group's activities depend on safety and actual conditions.

The complete tour includes domestic flights, transfers, excursions and accompaniment along the route. The confirmed inclusions and exclusions are listed on the [12-day itinerary page](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/). Do not apply its conditions to a nonexistent separate lake tour.

## Questions about tours to Lake Maracaibo

### On which day can travelers observe Catatumbo lightning?

On **day 8** of the [12-day Venezuela tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/). Nighttime observation is scheduled after arrival and check-in at camp. The group continues its journey the following day.

### Is lightning visible every night?

No. Catatumbo has a high average thunderstorm frequency, but clouds and weather vary. Visibility of lightning on a particular night cannot be guaranteed.

### Do travelers stay at a hotel in the city of Maracaibo?

Under the current itinerary, they stay **in hammocks at Palafito camp** in the natural area near the southwestern shore of the lake. This is a different accommodation format.

### Is Lake Maracaibo part of the main itinerary?

Yes. The trip to the lake and overnight stay at camp are included in the main route, not added on a free day.

### Can I see animals in Los Llanos after Maracaibo?

Yes. The route continues via [Barinas](/venezuela/place/barinas/) to [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/), where nature outings with local guides are scheduled.
